\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تصدیق} \ur{کرنا} (tasdīq karnā)}{تصدیق کرنا (tasdīq karnā)}]{\ur{تصدیق} \ur{کرنا} (tasdīq karnā) — to confirm}

\label{lesson:UR-C337-tasdiq-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a document, then the Urdu for genuine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تصدیق} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{تصدیق} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{tasdīq karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to confirm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پولیس} \ur{نے} \ur{اس} \ur{خبر} \ur{کی} \ur{تصدیق} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polīs ne is khabar kī tasdīq kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police confirmed the news.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{خبر} \ur{کی} \ur{تصدیق} \ur{کی}, \emph{us ne khabar kī tasdīq kī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تصدیق} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{tasdīq karnā}) is built from \emph{tasdīq}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taṣdīq}, \textquotedblleft{}declaring something true\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasdīq karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasdīq karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{polīs ne is khabar kī tasdīq kī.} — The police confirmed the news.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a document, then the Urdu for genuine, then say \emph{tasdīq karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تصدیق} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To confirm\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جھٹلانا} (jhuṭlānā)}{جھٹلانا (jhuṭlānā)}]{\ur{جھٹلانا} (jhuṭlānā) — to deny; to give the lie to}

\label{lesson:UR-C337-jhutlana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to confirm, then the Urdu for to acknowledge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جھٹلانا}}
\textbf{\ur{جھٹلانا}} — \emph{jhuṭlānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to deny; to give the lie to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{ہر} \ur{سچی} \ur{بات} \ur{کو} \ur{جھٹلاتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh har sachchī bāt ko jhuṭlātā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He denies everything that is true.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{خبر} \ur{کو} \ur{جھٹلایا}, \emph{us ne khabar ko jhuṭlāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جھٹلانا}} (\emph{jhuṭlānā}) is built on \textbf{\ur{جھوٹ}}, \textquotedblleft{}a lie\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{jhūṭhā}, \textquotedblleft{}lying, false\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*jhūṭṭha}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5407). To call a thing a lie.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhuṭlānā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to confirm, then the Urdu for to acknowledge, then say \emph{jhuṭlānā} again
\end{itemize}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for to acknowledge, then the Urdu for to give the lie to.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{غلط} \ur{فہمی} (ghalat-fahmī)}{غلط فہمی (ghalat-fahmī)}]{\ur{غلط} \ur{فہمی} (ghalat-fahmī) — a misunderstanding}

\label{lesson:UR-C337-ghalat-fahmi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to give the lie to, then the Urdu for to own up to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{غلط} \ur{فہمی}}
\textbf{\ur{غلط} \ur{فہمی}} — \emph{ghalat-fahmī} — \textquotedblleft{}a misunderstanding\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{ایک} \ur{غلط} \ur{فہمی} \ur{تھی،} \ur{کوئی} \ur{جھوٹ} \ur{نہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih ek ghalat-fahmī thī, koī jhūṭ nahīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It was a misunderstanding, not a lie.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{غلط} \ur{فہمی}} (\emph{ghalat-fahmī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{ghalat-fahmī}, \textquotedblleft{}a mistaken understanding\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\ur{غلط}}, \textquotedblleft{}wrong\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{fahmī}, \textquotedblleft{}understanding\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
